title: The weakest link · after the midterm

mood.title: Warm-up · how was this morning?
mood.prompt: Compared with the Week 9 practice, the midterm felt… Stand where you are. (About the morning, not your answers.)

deadline.title: Quick one · the deadline
deadline.prompt: When is your portfolio due? Walk to it.

weight.title: Quick one · how much it counts
weight.prompt: How much of the module is the portfolio? (About 3200 words.)

evidence.title: Evidenced, assumed or missing?
evidence.prompt: Six lines from a Campus Event portfolio, one at a time. Stand in your answer before the time runs out.
evidence.context: Evidenced: a reader can see it (a quote, a test result, a review note, a log). Assumed: you say it, but nothing shows it yet. Missing: the link isn't there.

rows.text: Test log: 14 passed, 1 failed. The failure is linked to the booking requirement.
I wrote a test plan for cancelling a booking.
The diagram shows that payments stay inside one component.
Nothing checks yet what happens when an event is full.
A classmate's review note quotes the requirement and asks about the waiting list.
The code is good quality because I followed the style guide.

passage.title: Which passage helps a reader decide?
passage.prompt: Read both, then walk to the one you would keep.
passage.context:
A: “Accessibility is important. The system will use good design, coding standards, and thorough testing. This will ensure that all users can book events.”

B: “The booking requirement includes keyboard-only use. Keep the booking controls in a predictable focus order and verify the complete journey, including error recovery, without a mouse. Until that check has been performed, keyboard access remains an unverified claim.”

options: It names a check and what isn't shown yet

promise.title: Spot the promise
promise.prompt: One line promises something nobody can check. Click the line you would cut.
promise.code:
Requirement: a student can cancel a booking up to one hour before the event.
Design: cancelling frees the seat and tells the first person on the waiting list.
This will make sure that no seat is ever wasted.
Check: a test cancels a booking for a full event; the waiting list moves up.
Not shown yet: a cancellation that arrives exactly one hour before.

ask.title: Peer review on 11 December
ask.prompt: You bring one passage. Which question gets you useful feedback? Walk to it.
options: Does this check address the failure I identified?
A classmate can answer it from one passage

rewrite.title: Optional · in pairs, fix the promise
rewrite.prompt: Rewrite line 3 as a check and its limit. One or two sentences.
rewrite.context:
The passage from “Spot the promise”:
1. Requirement: a student can cancel a booking up to one hour before the event.
2. Design: cancelling frees the seat and tells the first person on the waiting list.
3. This will make sure that no seat is ever wasted.  ← the promise
4. Check: a test cancels a booking for a full event; the waiting list moves up.
5. Not shown yet: a cancellation that arrives exactly one hour before.
rubric: Names something a reader could check (a test, a log, a count)
States what is still not shown, or where the check stops
rewrite.example: ==①A test fills an event, cancels one booking and expects the waiting list to move up.== ==②It does not yet cover a cancellation at the one-hour limit.==

debug.title: Next Monday
debug.prompt: If the fault disappears, did we debug it?

trophies.name: 12 January, 16:00
trophies.text: Portfolio: 80% of the module, about 3200 words, due Tuesday 12 January 2027 at 16:00.

trophies.name: Evidence lens
trophies.text: Evidenced means a reader can see it. A planned test is not a passed test; a diagram is not proof.
trophies.example: Mark each link E, A or M, then pick the next action that produces evidence.

trophies.name: Cut the promise
trophies.text: Keep the reason, the check and the limit. Cut what only promises.
trophies.example: “This will ensure all users can book” → which check, and what isn't shown yet?

trophies.name: One bounded question
trophies.text: On 11 December bring one passage, the decision it supports, and one question a classmate can answer.
